Wastewater and infection renewal ​

The data are CDC's public simulated example: wastewater RNA concentrations from a catchment of 400,000 people and daily hospital admissions in a state of 3,000,000 people. We use site 1 and the first 35 calendar days, from 1 September through 5 October 2023. Each wastewater record carries its sampling date, laboratory and detection limit; hospital records occupy a separate daily axis. The remaining state population has no wastewater observations. These are synthetic observations published by CDC's ww-inference-model, not measurements from a named community. The input tables and their exact source revision are linked under Reproduce.

Model ​

A shared weekly log reproduction number drives daily infection renewal. Each subpopulation follows that reference with its own stationary AR(1) deviation. Recent infections contribute infectiousness through a fixed generation-interval probability mass function. A feedback term attenuates the reproduction number as recent incidence increases:

Λk,t=∑s≥1gsIk,t−s,Ik,t=exp⁡(ℓt+δk,t−γΛk,t)Λk,t.

Here incidence is a daily population fraction. The reference has zero subpopulation deviation; its trajectory therefore anchors the hierarchy. Fifty unobserved days provide an exponentially seeded history before the first observation. Seven further days allow the fitted process to continue into a forecast. Neither the unobserved history nor the forecast contributes an extra observation likelihood.

The renewal recurrence is an ordinary StanBlocks function. This is the code the model calls, read from its source during the build:

julia
    renewal_feedback(logRt::vector[nt], g::vector[ng], gamma::real, I0::real,
                     r::real, n_seed::int)::vector[nt] = begin
        I::vector[nt]
        for t in 1:nt
            if t <= n_seed
                I[t] = I0 * exp(r * (t - 1))
            else
                conv = 0.0
                for s in 1:ng
                    prev = t - s >= 1 ? I[t - s] : 0.0
                    conv = conv + g[s] * prev
                end
                Rt = exp(logRt[t]) * exp(-gamma * conv)
                I[t] = Rt * conv
            end
        end
        I
    end

The @brm declaration keeps the population hierarchy, priors and observation families together. Its plate produces the infection trajectory of each subpopulation. Separate indexing arrays then connect each observed sample to the appropriate day, catchment and laboratory. Repeated measurements can share one latent infection value without duplicating that state.

function cdc_ww_brm_model(df = cdc_ww_brm_fixture())
    @brm df begin
        # Shared epidemic parameters. `dar` owns the zero-start differenced-AR
        # innovations while the intercept remains the initial weekly log-Rᵘ level.
        gamma       ~ LogNormal(-4.0, 0.5)
        phi_delta   ~ Beta(2.0, 8.0)
        sigma_delta ~ Exponential(4.0)
        log10_g     ~ Normal(12.0, 1.0)
        t_peak      ~ LogNormal(log(4.0), 0.25)
        viral_peak  ~ Normal(6.0, 1.0)
        shed_tail   ~ LogNormal(log(14.0), 0.3)
        dur_shed = t_peak + shed_tail
        shedding = viral_shedding_trajectory(t_peak, viral_peak, dur_shed, nsh)

        log_ru_week ~ 1 + dar(week_grid; p = 1)
        effect(log_ru_week, Intercept) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        log_ru = weekly_expand(log_ru_week, week_idx)

        # Hierarchical incidence and initial growth are defined over the latent
        # subpopulation axis, including the uncovered reference population.
        logit_I0      ~ 1 + (1 | initial | subpopulation)
        initial_growth ~ 1 + (1 | growth | subpopulation)
        effect(logit_I0, Intercept) ~ Normal(-9.0, 1.0)
        effect(initial_growth, Intercept) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.05)
        sd(:, initial) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.75)
        sd(:, growth) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.05)

        # The plate produces latent trajectories only, one per subpopulation.
        # Observation frames are mapped onto this matrix after the plate.
        @plate for k in eachindex(logit_I0)
            eps_d ~ Normal(zeros(n_total), 1.0)             # this subpopulation's daily innovations
            delta_k = ar1_dev(eps_d, phi_delta, sigma_delta)
            log_rt_k = log_ru .+ (1.0 - is_reference[k]) .* delta_k
            I_mat[k] = renewal_from_first_observed(log_rt_k, g, gamma,
                                                   logistic(logit_I0[k]), initial_growth[k], uot)
        end

        # Sparse wastewater records have independent time, subpopulation, lab
        # and record-specific LOD mappings. Multiple labs may observe the same
        # catchment/time pair; the reference population may have no records.
        log_lab_mod ~ 0 + (1 | ww_scale | ww_lab)
        log_sigma_ww ~ 1 + (1 | ww_noise | ww_lab)
        effect(log_sigma_ww, Intercept) ~ Normal(log(0.35), 0.5)
        sd(:, ww_scale) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, ww_noise) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.35)
        ww_mu = ww_expected_log(I_mat, shedding, ww_time, ww_subpop, ww_obs_lab,
                                log_lab_mod, log10_g, mwpd)
        ww_sigma = gather_exp(log_sigma_ww, ww_obs_lab)
        ww_log_conc ~ censored(Normal(ww_mu, ww_sigma); lower = ww_lod)

        # jurisdiction aggregate infections (population-weighted across subpops)
        I_agg = wsum(I_mat, w)

        # Count-stream module. Each stream gets a hierarchical rate center and a
        # stationary weekly AR deviation. Observation rows can be daily or span
        # arbitrary inclusive intervals and can map different latent catchments.
        phi_count ~ Beta(2.0, 8.0)
        sigma_count ~ Exponential(20.0)
        count_rate_center ~ 1 + (1 | count_rate | count_stream)
        effect(count_rate_center, Intercept) ~ Normal(-4.6, 0.3)
        sd(:, count_rate) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        @plate for s in eachindex(count_rate_center)
            eps_count ~ Normal(zeros(n_weeks), 1.0)         # this stream's weekly innovations
            count_rate_week[s] = count_rate_center[s] .+ ar1_dev(eps_count, phi_count, sigma_count)
        end
        count_rate_daily = weekly_expand_columns(count_rate_week, week_idx)
        dow_share ~ Dirichlet(7, 5.0)
        dow_effect = scale_simplex(dow_share, 7.0)
        log_phi_count ~ 1 + (1 | count_dispersion | count_stream)
        effect(log_phi_count, Intercept) ~ Normal(log(15.0), 0.5)
        sd(:, count_dispersion) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        count_mu = count_interval_mean(I_mat, count_subpop_weights, count_delay,
                                       count_rate_daily, count_start, count_stop,
                                       count_obs_stream, dow, dow_effect,
                                       count_population)
        count_phi = gather_exp(log_phi_count, count_obs_stream)
        count ~ NegativeBinomial2(count_mu, count_phi)

        # Forecast contract: named deterministic carriers use the same fitted
        # latent state and observation mappings but are not calibration outcomes.
        forecast_infections = take_window(I_agg, uot + nt + 1, ht)
        forecast_count_mean = count_interval_mean(
            I_mat, count_subpop_weights, count_delay, count_rate_daily,
            forecast_count_start, forecast_count_stop,
            forecast_count_obs_stream, dow, dow_effect, count_population)
        forecast_ww_log_mean = ww_expected_log(
            I_mat, shedding, forecast_ww_time, forecast_ww_subpop,
            forecast_ww_obs_lab, log_lab_mod, log10_g, mwpd)
    end
end

function wastewater_public_model(data=wastewater_public_data())
    cdc_ww_brm_model(data)
end

"""
Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
`z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
"""
brm_group_effects(g) = begin
        tau[1:1] .~ restricted.(Normal(0.0, 0.75), 0.0, Inf)
        z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] .~ Normal.(0, 1)
        return z .* tau[1]
    end

"""
Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
`z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
"""
brm_group_effects_(g) = begin
        tau[1:1] .~ restricted.(Normal(0.0, 0.05), 0.0, Inf)
        z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] .~ Normal.(0, 1)
        return z .* tau[1]
    end

"""
Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
`z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
"""
brm_group_effects__(g) = begin
        tau[1:1] .~ restricted.(Normal(0.0, 0.5), 0.0, Inf)
        z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] .~ Normal.(0, 1)
        return z .* tau[1]
    end

"""
Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
`z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
"""
brm_group_effects___(g) = begin
        tau[1:1] .~ restricted.(Normal(0.0, 0.35), 0.0, Inf)
        z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] .~ Normal.(0, 1)
        return z .* tau[1]
    end

"""
A differenced AR(1) level path over `T` steps (`dar`).

Draws the persistence `beta` and innovation scale `sigma` from their priors.
The path starts at `level[1] = increment[1] = 0`; then
`increment[t] = beta * increment[t - 1] + sigma * innovation` with
`innovation ~ Normal(0, 1)`, and `level[t] = level[t - 1] + increment[t]`.
Returns the level path `level`.
"""
brm_differenced_ar1(T) = begin
        beta ~ truncated(Normal(0.5, 0.2), 0, 1)
        sigma ~ HalfNormal(0.2)
        @scan begin
                level[1] = 0.0
                increment[1] = 0.0
                for t = 2:T
                    innovation ~ Normal(0, 1)
                    increment[t] = beta * increment[t - 1] + sigma * innovation
                    level[t] = level[t - 1] + increment[t]
                end
            end
        return level
    end

"""
A plate's cell values, concatenated in cell order.

Scalar cells are returned as they are; vector cells are joined with
`reduce(vcat, cells)` (an empty vector when there are no cells).
"""
ReactiveKernels.@kernel(flatten_cells(cells) = begin
            values = if eltype(cells) <: Number
                    cells
                else
                    if eltype(cells) <: AbstractVector
                        if isempty(cells)
                            (eltype(eltype(cells)))[]
                        else
                            reduce(vcat, cells)
                        end
                    else
                        brm_flatten_cells(cells)
                    end
                end
            return values
        end)

    dur_shed = t_peak .+ shed_tail

    ww_sigma = gather_exp(log_sigma_ww, ww_obs_lab)
    dow_effect = scale_simplex(dow_share, 7.0)
    count_phi = gather_exp(log_phi_count, count_obs_stream)

    ww_mu = ww_expected_log(I_mat_cells, shedding, ww_time, ww_subpop, ww_obs_lab, log_lab_mod, log10_g, mwpd)
    I_agg = wsum(I_mat_cells, w)
    forecast_infections = take_window(I_agg, .+(uot, nt, 1), ht)
    forecast_ww_log_mean = ww_expected_log(I_mat_cells, shedding, forecast_ww_time, forecast_ww_subpop, forecast_ww_obs_lab, log_lab_mod, log10_g, mwpd)

            eps_count_cell = eps_count[i_]
            count_rate_week_cells[i_] = count_rate_center[i_] .+ ar1_dev(eps_count_cell, phi_count, sigma_count)
        end
    count_rate_week = flatten_cells(count_rate_week_cells)
    count_rate_daily = weekly_expand_columns(count_rate_week_cells, week_idx)
    count_mu = count_interval_mean(I_mat_cells, count_subpop_weights, count_delay, count_rate_daily, count_start, count_stop, count_obs_stream, dow, dow_effect, count_population)
    forecast_count_mean = count_interval_mean(I_mat_cells, count_subpop_weights, count_delay, count_rate_daily, forecast_count_start, forecast_count_stop, forecast_count_obs_stream, dow, dow_effect, count_population)
    ww_log_conc .~ censored.(Normal.(ww_mu, ww_sigma), ww_lod, Inf)
    count .~ NegativeBinomial2.(count_mu, count_phi)
end

functions {
vector viral_shedding_trajectory(
    real t_peak,
    real viral_peak,
    real duration_shedding,
    int n
) {
    vector[n] s;
    real growth = (viral_peak / t_peak);
    real wane = (viral_peak / (duration_shedding - t_peak));
    for(t in 1:n) {
        if((t <= t_peak)) {
            s[t] = exp((log(10.0) * growth * t));
        } else {
            real log10_load = ((viral_peak + (wane * t_peak)) - (wane * t));
            s[t] = exp((log(10.0) * ((log10_load < 0.0) ? 0.0 : log10_load)));
        }
    }
    return (s / sum(s));
}
// Form a matrix by concatenating the supplied columns in order.
matrix hcat(vector x) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    return to_matrix(x, n, 1);
}
vector differenced_ar1_path(
    real beta,
    real sigma,
    vector z
) {
    int n = dims(z)[1];
    vector[(n + 1)] x = rep_vector(0.0, (n + 1));
    real increment = 0.0;
    if((n > 0)) {
        for(t in 1:n) {
            increment = ((beta * increment) + (sigma * z[t]));
            x[(t + 1)] = (x[t] + increment);
        }
    }
    return x;
}
vector weekly_expand(
    vector x,
    array[] int week_idx
) {
    int nt = dims(week_idx)[1];
    return x[week_idx];
}
vector gather_exp(vector x, array[] int idx) {
    int n = dims(idx)[1];
    return exp(x[idx]);
}
vector scale_simplex(vector x, real scale) {
    int K = dims(x)[1];

}
// Return one normalized log probability per observation, broadcasting distribution parameters elementwise.
vector normal_lpdfs(

) {

}
vector jbroadcasted_normal_lpdfs(
    vector x1,
    vector x2,
    real x3
) {
    int n = dims(x1)[1];
    vector[n] rv;
    for(i in 1:n) {

    }

}
// Return the normalized log probability for a single observation.
real normal_lpdfs(

    real args3
) {
    return normal_lpdf(args1 | args2, args3);
}
// Read element i of a container used in elementwise broadcasting.
real broadcasted_getindex(vector x, int i) {

// Draw independent values of the requested size, broadcasting scalar parameters and preserving the requested container type.
vector normal_vector_rng(

) {

vector ar1_dev(
    vector eps,
    real phi,
    real sigma
) {
    int nt = dims(eps)[1];
    vector[nt] d;
    d[1] = ((sigma * eps[1]) / sqrt((1.0 - square(phi))));
    for(t in 2:nt) {
        d[t] = ((phi * d[(t - 1)]) + (sigma * eps[t]));
    }
    return d;
}
vector renewal_from_first_observed(
    vector logRt,
    vector g,
    real gamma,
    real i_first_obs,
    real growth,
    int uot
) {
    int nt = dims(logRt)[1];
    return renewal_feedback(logRt, g, gamma, exp((log(i_first_obs) - (uot * growth))), growth, uot);
}
vector renewal_feedback(
    vector logRt,
    vector g,
    real gamma,
    real I0,
    real r,
    int n_seed
) {
    int nt = dims(logRt)[1];
    int ng = dims(g)[1];
    vector[nt] I;
    for(t in 1:nt) {
        if((t <= n_seed)) {
            I[t] = (I0 * exp((r * (t - 1))));
        } else {
            real conv = 0.0;
            for(s in 1:ng) {
                real prev = (((t - s) >= 1) ? I[(t - s)] : 0.0);
                conv = (conv + (g[s] * prev));
            }
            real Rt = (exp(logRt[t]) * exp(((-gamma) * conv)));
            I[t] = (Rt * conv);
        }
    }
    return I;
}
vector ww_expected_log(
    matrix I_mat,
    vector sh,
    array[] int sample_time,
    array[] int sample_subpop,

    vector log_lab_mod,

    real mwpd
) {

    if (dims(sample_lab)[1] != n) reject("ww_expected_log: dim mismatch — `sample_lab` dim 1 (= ", dims(sample_lab)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `sample_time` dim 1. `n` sizes: `sample_time` dim 1 (= ", dims(sample_time)[1], "), `sample_subpop` dim 1 (= ", dims(sample_subpop)[1], "), `sample_lab` dim 1 (= ", dims(sample_lab)[1], ").");
    vector[n] out;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        real shed = 0.0;
        for(lag in 1:nsh) {
            int t = ((sample_time[i] - lag) + 1);
            shed = (shed + ((t >= 1) ? (sh[lag] * I_mat[t, sample_subpop[i]]) : 0.0));
        }
        out[i] = ((((log(10.0) * log10_g) + log((shed + 1.0e-8))) - log(mwpd)) + log_lab_mod[sample_lab[i]]);

}

real lower_clamping_normal_lpdf(

// Return the censored log likelihood: log P(Y <= lo) at lo, the base log probability in the interior, and -infinity outside the limits.
real lower_clamping_normal_lpdf(
    real y,
    real lo,
    real args1,
    real args2
) {
    array[1] real rv;
    rv[1] = negative_infinity();

    } else {

            rv[1] = normal_lpdf(y | args1, args2);
        }
    }

}
// Compute log P(Y <= x) for a normal distribution, preserving small tail probabilities and handling infinite bounds directly.
real normal_lcdf_stable(
    real x,
    real loc,
    real scale
) {
    return (is_inf(x) ? ((x < 0) ? negative_infinity() : 0.0) : ((((x - loc) / scale) < -35) ? std_normal_lcdf_tail(((x - loc) / scale)) : ((((x - loc) / scale) <= 0) ? (log(erfc(((-(x - loc)) / (scale * sqrt(2.0))))) - log(2.0)) : log1m((0.5 * erfc(((x - loc) / (scale * sqrt(2.0)))))))));

// Approximate log Phi(z) in the far negative normal tail without underflowing the probability.
real std_normal_lcdf_tail(

) {

// Approximate log Phi(z) + z^2/2 in the far negative normal tail using the Mills expansion.
real std_normal_scaled_lcdf_tail(

) {
    real w = inv(square(z));

        ((-log((-z))) - 0.9189385332046728) +

vector jbroadcasted_lower_clamping_cell_rng_normal_rng(

// Draw from the base distribution and return max(Y, lo), placing out-of-range draws at their censoring limits.

) {

vector wsum(
    matrix I_mat,

) {

    if (dims(w)[1] != K) reject("wsum: dim mismatch — `w` dim 1 (= ", dims(w)[1], ") does not match `K` (= ", K, "), inferred from `I_mat` dim 2. `K` sizes: `I_mat` dim 2 (= ", dims(I_mat)[2], "), `w` dim 1 (= ", dims(w)[1], ").");

vector take_window(

) {

matrix weekly_expand_columns(

) {

    for(t in 1:nt) {

vector count_interval_mean(
    matrix I_mat,
    matrix subpop_weights,

    int K = dims(I_mat)[2];

    if (dims(logit_rate)[1] != nt) reject("count_interval_mean: dim mismatch — `logit_rate` dim 1 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[1], ") does not match `nt` (= ", nt, "), inferred from `I_mat` dim 1. `nt` sizes: `I_mat` dim 1 (= ", dims(I_mat)[1], "), `logit_rate` dim 1 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[1], "), `dow` dim 1 (= ", dims(dow)[1], ").");
    if (dims(dow)[1] != nt) reject("count_interval_mean: dim mismatch — `dow` dim 1 (= ", dims(dow)[1], ") does not match `nt` (= ", nt, "), inferred from `I_mat` dim 1. `nt` sizes: `I_mat` dim 1 (= ", dims(I_mat)[1], "), `logit_rate` dim 1 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[1], "), `dow` dim 1 (= ", dims(dow)[1], ").");
    if (dims(subpop_weights)[1] != K) reject("count_interval_mean: dim mismatch — `subpop_weights` dim 1 (= ", dims(subpop_weights)[1], ") does not match `K` (= ", K, "), inferred from `I_mat` dim 2. `K` sizes: `I_mat` dim 2 (= ", dims(I_mat)[2], "), `subpop_weights` dim 1 (= ", dims(subpop_weights)[1], ").");
    if (dims(delay)[2] != S) reject("count_interval_mean: dim mismatch — `delay` dim 2 (= ", dims(delay)[2], ") does not match `S` (= ", S, "), inferred from `subpop_weights` dim 2. `S` sizes: `subpop_weights` dim 2 (= ", dims(subpop_weights)[2], "), `delay` dim 2 (= ", dims(delay)[2], "), `logit_rate` dim 2 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[2], "), `population` dim 1 (= ", dims(population)[1], ").");
    if (dims(logit_rate)[2] != S) reject("count_interval_mean: dim mismatch — `logit_rate` dim 2 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[2], ") does not match `S` (= ", S, "), inferred from `subpop_weights` dim 2. `S` sizes: `subpop_weights` dim 2 (= ", dims(subpop_weights)[2], "), `delay` dim 2 (= ", dims(delay)[2], "), `logit_rate` dim 2 (= ", dims(logit_rate)[2], "), `population` dim 1 (= ", dims(population)[1], ").");

def _rk_order_key_np(x):
    # Julia's isless order of an array as sortable keys: a float is an integer
    # key, -0.0 before 0.0 and every NaN last, equal for values isequal treats
    # as equal. Integer and string arrays are their own keys.
    x = np.asarray(x)
    if x.dtype.kind != "f":
        return x
    bits = np.where(np.isnan(x), np.nan, x).astype(np.float64).view(np.int64)
    return np.where(bits < 0, bits ^ np.int64(0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF), bits)


def _rk_unique_np(x):
    # Julia's unique of a vector: the first value of each isequal class, in
    # order.
    x = np.asarray(x)
    _, first = np.unique(_rk_order_key_np(x), return_index=True)
    return x[np.sort(first)]


def _rk_sort_np(x):
    # Julia's sort of a vector: ascending in isless order, equal values in
    # their order.
    x = np.asarray(x)
    return x[np.argsort(_rk_order_key_np(x), kind="stable")]


def _brm_sorted_labels_np(source):
    labels = _rk_unique_np(source)
    sorted_ = _rk_sort_np(labels)
    return sorted_


def _brm_fit_levels_np(source):
    value = _brm_sorted_labels_np(source)
    levels = value
    return levels


def _rk_dict_key(x):
    if isinstance(x, tuple):
        return (1, tuple(map(_rk_dict_key, x)))
    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
        return (2, x.shape, tuple(map(_rk_dict_key, x.ravel(order="F"))))
    if isinstance(x, (complex, np.complexfloating)):
        if x.imag == 0 and not np.signbit(x.imag):
            return _rk_dict_key(x.real)
        return (3, _rk_dict_key(x.real), _rk_dict_key(x.imag))
    if isinstance(x, (float, np.floating)):
        if np.isnan(x):
            return (4,)
        if x == 0 and np.signbit(x):
            return (5,)
    return (0, x)

class _RKDict:
    def __init__(self, pairs=()):
        self.data = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            self[key] = value

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.data)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        return _rk_dict_key(key) in self.data

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        return self.data[_rk_dict_key(key)][1]

    def __setitem__(self, key, value):
        self.data[_rk_dict_key(key)] = (key, value)

    def get(self, key, default):
        item = self.data.get(_rk_dict_key(key))
        return default if item is None else item[1]

    def setdefault(self, key, default):
        return self.data.setdefault(_rk_dict_key(key), (key, default))[1]

    def pop(self, key, default):
        item = self.data.pop(_rk_dict_key(key), None)
        return default if item is None else item[1]

    def items(self):
        return self.data.values()

    def keys(self):
        return (item[0] for item in self.items())

    def values(self):
        return (item[1] for item in self.items())

    def copy(self):
        return _RKDict(self.items())


def _brm_level_indices_np(labels, source):
    value = _brm_fit_levels_np(source)
    levels = value
    lookup = _RKDict()
    for k in range(1, len(levels) + 1):
        lookup[levels[k - 1]] = k
    indices = np.zeros((len(labels),), dtype=np.int64)
    for r in range(1, len(labels) + 1):
        position = lookup.get(labels[r - 1], 0)
        if position == 0:
            raise ValueError("".join([str("RK backend: group label `"), str(labels[r - 1]), str("` is not one of the "), str(len(levels)), str(" fitted levels. A replay keeps the fitted levels of every grouping it does not resample; name the grouping in `resample_groups` to take the new data's own levels.")]))
        indices[r - 1] = position
    return indices


def _rk_broadcast_shape_np(*shapes):
    # Julia's Broadcast.broadcast_shape of axes tuples: a length-1 axis
    # stretches, the other lengths must agree.
    out = []
    for d in range(max([0] + [len(s) for s in shapes])):
        lengths = set(len(s[d]) for s in shapes if d < len(s)) - {1}
        if len(lengths) > 1:
            raise ValueError("DimensionMismatch: arrays could not be broadcast to a common size")
        out.append(range(1, (lengths.pop() if lengths else 1) + 1))
    return tuple(out)


def _rk_levels_np(x):
    arr = np.asarray(x)
    values = sorted(set(v for v in arr.tolist() if v is not None))
    return np.array(values, dtype=object if arr.dtype == object else arr.dtype)


class StaticInt(int):
    """An integer of the prepared data that sets a shape.

    It is an `int` everywhere, and `jax.jit` treats it as static, so the
    functions jit with the prepared data as arguments; a new value traces
    them again.
    """

    def __repr__(self):
        return "StaticInt(%d)" % int(self)


jax.tree_util.register_pytree_node(StaticInt, lambda s: ((), int(s)), lambda v, _: StaticInt(v))


def _rk_pad_rows(rows, dtype, rank=1):
    # A ragged value as the functions take it: the padded array (each row
    # repeats its last entry; an empty row is zeros), the lengths, and the
    # positions of the valid entries in the flattened padded array, whose
    # length is the total. `dtype` is the element type the program declares,
    # so an empty row (`[]`) keeps an integer column integer.
    rows = [np.asarray(r, dtype=dtype) for r in rows]
    # One length per cell describes its first axis. Other axes retain a
    # common shape; independently ragged axes need separate extents.
    tail = rows[0].shape[1:] if rows else (1,) * (rank - 1)
    if any(r.ndim != rank or r.shape[1:] != tail for r in rows):
        raise ValueError("ragged cells need their declared rank and common trailing dimensions")
    lengths = np.asarray([r.shape[0] for r in rows], dtype=np.int64)
    width = max([1 if rank > 1 and not rows else 0] + [int(n) for n in lengths])
    padded = np.stack([np.pad(r, ((0, width - r.shape[0]),) + ((0, 0),) * (rank - 1),
                             mode="edge") if r.shape[0] > 0
                       else np.zeros((width,) + tail, dtype=dtype) for r in rows]) if rows else np.zeros((0, width) + tail, dtype=dtype)
    flat = np.flatnonzero(np.arange(width)[None, :] < lengths[:, None])
    return padded, lengths, flat


def _rk_columns_np(value, dtypes):
    # An array of tuples as the functions take it: the tuple of its columns,
    # one NumPy array per field, from its columns or from a list of its rows.
    n = len(dtypes)
    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray) and value.dtype == object:
        return tuple(np.asarray([r[k] for r in value.ravel(order="F")], dtype=d)
                     .reshape(value.shape, order="F") for k, d in enumerate(dtypes))
    if isinstance(value, tuple) and len(value) == n and \
            not any(isinstance(c, (tuple, list)) for c in value):
        return tuple(np.asarray(c, dtype=d) for c, d in zip(value, dtypes))
    if isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(r, tuple) and len(r) == n for r in value):
        return tuple(np.asarray([r[k] for r in value], dtype=d) for k, d in enumerate(dtypes))
    raise TypeError("an array of %d-tuples is the tuple of its columns or an array/list of its rows, not %r"
                    % (n, type(value).__name__))


def _rk_columns(value, dtypes):
    # A vector of tuples as the functions read it: the tuple of its columns,
    # as `prepare_data` returns it, each a JAX array, which a cell can index by
    # its traced index (a NumPy array cannot be).
    if not (isinstance(value, tuple) and len(value) == len(dtypes)) or \
            any(isinstance(c, (tuple, list)) for c in value):
        raise TypeError("a vector of %d-tuples is passed as the tuple of its columns, "
                        "as prepare_data returns it" % len(dtypes))
    return tuple(jnp.asarray(c, dtype=d) for c, d in zip(value, dtypes))


@jax.custom_jvp
def _rk_affine_logistic(x1, x2, x3):
    return x1 + (x2 - x1) / (1 + jnp.exp(-x3))


def _affine_logistic_partials_1(x1, x2, x3):
    q = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    return (x1 + (x2 - x1) / (1 + jnp.exp(-x3)), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, q, 1.0) / (1 + q))


def _affine_logistic_partials_2(x1, x2, x3):
    q = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    return (x1 + (x2 - x1) / (1 + jnp.exp(-x3)), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, 1.0, q) / (1 + q))


def _affine_logistic_partials_3(x1, x2, x3):
    q = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    q_2 = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    return (x1 + (x2 - x1) / (1 + jnp.exp(-x3)), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, q_2, 1.0) / (1 + q_2), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, 1.0, q) / (1 + q))


def _affine_logistic_partials_4(x1, x2, x3):
    q = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    q_2 = jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(x3))
    return (x1 + (x2 - x1) / (1 + jnp.exp(-x3)), (x2 - x1) * (jnp.where(x3 >= 0, 1.0, q) / (1 + q)) * (jnp.where(x3 >= 0, q_2, 1.0) / (1 + q_2)), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, q_2, 1.0) / (1 + q_2), jnp.where(x3 >= 0, 1.0, q) / (1 + q))


def _affine_logistic_jvp(primals, tangents):
    active = tuple(not isinstance(t, jax.custom_derivatives.SymbolicZero) for t in tangents)
    mask = sum((1 << i) for i, a in enumerate(active) if a)
    if mask == 0:
        value = _rk_affine_logistic(*primals)
        return value, jnp.zeros_like(value)
    if mask == 1:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_1(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[0]
    if mask == 2:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_2(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[1]
    if mask == 3:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_3(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[0] + values[2] * tangents[1]
    if mask == 4:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_4(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[2]
    if mask == 5:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_4(*primals)
        return values[0], values[2] * tangents[0] + values[1] * tangents[2]
    if mask == 6:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_4(*primals)
        return values[0], values[3] * tangents[1] + values[1] * tangents[2]
    if mask == 7:
        values = _affine_logistic_partials_4(*primals)
        return values[0], values[2] * tangents[0] + values[3] * tangents[1] + values[1] * tangents[2]
_rk_affine_logistic.defjvp(_affine_logistic_jvp, symbolic_zeros=True)


def _rk_simplex_constrain_logjac(u, lo, hi):
    # RKPPL stick-breaking simplex of u[lo:hi] and its log-Jacobian.
    v = u[lo - 1:hi]
    K = hi - lo + 2
    z = 1.0 / (1.0 + jnp.exp(-(v + jnp.log((K - jnp.arange(1, K)).astype(v.dtype)))))
    l = jnp.log1p(-z)
    lr = jnp.cumsum(jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros(1, dtype=v.dtype), l]))
    return (jnp.exp(lr) * jnp.concatenate([z, jnp.ones(1, dtype=v.dtype)]),
            jnp.sum(lr[:K - 1] + jnp.log(z) + l))


def _normal_direct_interval(a: ArrayLike, b: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_normal_direct_interval` from its authored source."""
    return (a >= -8) & (b <= 8) & (b - a >= 0.125)


def _function(a: ArrayLike, b: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `function` from its kernel plan."""
    crosses_zero = (a < 0) & (b > 0)
    qa = 0.5 * ssp.erfc((a if a >= 0 else -a) / np.sqrt(2.0))
    qb = 0.5 * ssp.erfc((b if (True if b > 0 else a >= 0) else -b) / np.sqrt(2.0))
    outside = qa + qb
    mass = (1 - outside if crosses_zero else (qa - qb if a >= 0 else qb - qa))
    value = (np.log1p(-outside) if crosses_zero else np.log(mass))
    return value


def _standardized(location: ArrayLike, scale: ArrayLike, log_scale: ArrayLike, x: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standardized` from its kernel plan."""
    standardized = (x - location) / (1.0 if (x == location if scale == 0 else False) else scale)
    return standardized


def _normal_scaled_tail(z: ArrayLike, w: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_normal_scaled_tail` from its authored source."""
    return (ssp.erfcx(w) if z < 0 else 0.0)


def _normal_logcdf_from_tail(z: ArrayLike, w: ArrayLike, scaled: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_normal_logcdf_from_tail` from its authored source."""
    return (np.log(scaled) - w ** 2 - np.log(2.0) if z < 0 else np.log1p(-0.5 * ssp.erfc(-w)))


def _standard_logcdf(standard_z: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standard_logcdf` from its kernel plan."""
    normal_scaled_tail = _normal_scaled_tail(standard_z, -standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0))
    normal_logcdf_from_tail = _normal_logcdf_from_tail(standard_z, -standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0), normal_scaled_tail)
    standard_logcdf = normal_logcdf_from_tail
    return standard_logcdf


def _standardized_2(location: ArrayLike, scale: ArrayLike, log_scale: ArrayLike, x: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standardized_2` from its kernel plan."""
    standardized = (x - location) / (1.0 if (x == location if scale == 0 else False) else scale)
    return standardized


def _normal_scaled_tail_2(z: ArrayLike, w: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_normal_scaled_tail` from its authored source."""
    return (ssp.erfcx(w) if z < 0 else 0.0)


def _normal_logcdf_from_tail_2(z: ArrayLike, w: ArrayLike, scaled: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_normal_logcdf_from_tail` from its authored source."""
    return (np.log(scaled) - w ** 2 - np.log(2.0) if z < 0 else np.log1p(-0.5 * ssp.erfc(-w)))


def _standard_logccdf(standard_z: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standard_logccdf` from its kernel plan."""
    normal_scaled_tail_2 = _normal_scaled_tail_2(-standard_z, --standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0), active)
    normal_logcdf_from_tail_2 = _normal_logcdf_from_tail_2(-standard_z, --standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0), normal_scaled_tail_2, active)
    standard_logccdf = normal_logcdf_from_tail_2
    return standard_logccdf


def _rk_log1mexp(x):
    # log(1 - exp(x)) for x <= 0 (LogExpFunctions.log1mexp).
    small = x < -0.6931471805599453
    safe_small = jnp.where(small, x, -1.0)
    safe_large = jnp.where(small, -1.0, x)
    return jnp.where(small, jnp.log1p(-jnp.exp(safe_small)),
                     jnp.log(-jnp.expm1(safe_large)))


def _standardized_3(location: ArrayLike, scale: ArrayLike, log_scale: ArrayLike, x: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standardized_3` from its kernel plan."""
    standardized = (x - location) / (1.0 if (x == location if scale == 0 else False) else scale)
    return standardized


def _standard_logcdf_2(standard_z: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `standard_logcdf_2` from its kernel plan."""
    normal_scaled_tail_2 = _normal_scaled_tail_2(standard_z, -standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0), active)
    normal_logcdf_from_tail_2 = _normal_logcdf_from_tail_2(standard_z, -standard_z / np.sqrt(2.0), normal_scaled_tail_2, active)
    standard_logcdf = normal_logcdf_from_tail_2
    return standard_logcdf


def _logpdf(x: ArrayLike, location: ArrayLike, scale: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `logpdf` from its kernel plan."""
    log_scale = np.log(scale)
    standardized = (x - location) / jnp.where((x == location if scale == 0 else False), 1.0, scale)
    standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * standardized ** 2
    logpdf = standard_logpdf - jnp.where((x != location if scale == 0 else False), 0.0, log_scale)
    return logpdf


def brm_differenced_ar1_density(
    ppl_scan_z_level: ArrayLike,
    beta: ArrayLike,
    sigma: ArrayLike,
    *,
    outputs: tuple[str, ...],
) -> dict:
    """A differenced AR(1) level path over `T` steps (`dar`).

    Draws the persistence `beta` and innovation scale `sigma` from their priors.
    The path starts at `level[1] = increment[1] = 0`; then
    `increment[t] = beta * increment[t - 1] + sigma * innovation` with
    `innovation ~ Normal(0, 1)`, and `level[t] = level[t - 1] + increment[t]`.
    Returns the level path `level`.
    """
    results = {}
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_scan_init_level_1", "ppl_scan_rest_level", "level")):
        ppl_scan_init_level_1 = 0.0
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_scan_rest_level", "level")):
        ppl_scan_init_increment_1 = 0.0
        scan_argument = (ppl_scan_init_level_1, ppl_scan_init_increment_1)
        scan_argument_2 = jnp.arange(2, 15)
        prefix_stop = 13
        if not (prefix_stop <= ppl_scan_z_level.size):
            raise ValueError("BoundsError: prefix exceeds array length")
        scan_argument_3 = ppl_scan_z_level[:max(prefix_stop, 0)]
        def ppl_scan_outputs_level_step(carry, xs):
            ppl_scan_index, ppl_e1 = xs
            ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_increment = beta * carry[1] + sigma * ppl_e1
            ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_level = carry[0] + ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_increment
            ppl_next = (ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_level, ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_increment)
            scan_output = (ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_level, ppl_scan_n_dar_log_ru_week_week_grid_level_increment)
            return ppl_next, scan_output
        scan_result = jax.lax.scan(ppl_scan_outputs_level_step, scan_argument, (scan_argument_2, scan_argument_3))[1] if 1 <= scan_argument_2.shape[0] else (jnp.zeros((0,), dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.zeros((0,), dtype=jnp.float64),)
        ppl_scan_outputs_level = scan_result
        def ppl_scan_rest_level_cell(scan_row):
            plate_value = scan_row[0]
            return plate_value
        ppl_scan_rest_level = (jnp.zeros(ppl_scan_outputs_level[0].shape[:1], dtype=jnp.float64) if 0 in ppl_scan_outputs_level[0].shape[:1] else jax.vmap(ppl_scan_rest_level_cell, in_axes=(0,))(ppl_scan_outputs_level))
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("level",)):
        level = jnp.concatenate([jnp.stack([ppl_scan_init_level_1]), ppl_scan_rest_level])
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_beta", "ppl_prior_beta_logpdf")):
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_location = 0.5
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_scale = 0.2
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_log_scale = np.log(ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_scale)
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_logpdf_z = (beta - ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_location) / jnp.where((beta == ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_location if ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_scale == 0 else False), 1.0, ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_scale)
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_logpdf_z ** 2
        ppl_prior_beta_logpdf = ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_standard_logpdf - jnp.where((beta != ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_location if ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_scale == 0 else False), 0.0, ppl_prior_beta_logpdf_log_scale)
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_beta",)):
        if 0.2 > 0:
            normal_direct_interval = _normal_direct_interval((0.0 - 0.5) / 0.2, (1.0 - 0.5) / 0.2)
            value = normal_direct_interval
        else:
            value = False
        if value:
            function = _function((0.0 - 0.5) / 0.2, (1.0 - 0.5) / 0.2)
            value_17 = function
        else:
            log_scale = np.log(0.2)
            if (0.0 == 0.5 if 0.2 == 0 else False):
                value_2 = 1.0 / 0.2
            else:
                standardized = _standardized(0.5, 0.2, log_scale, 0.0)
                value_2 = standardized
            logcdf_z = value_2
            if 0.0 == -jnp.inf:
                value_4 = -jnp.inf
            else:
                if 0.0 == jnp.inf:
                    value_3 = 0.0
                else:
                    standard_logcdf = _standard_logcdf(logcdf_z)
                    value_3 = standard_logcdf
                value_4 = value_3
            def then_arm():

                    value_5 = standardized_2
                logccdf_z = value_5
                if 0.0 == jnp.inf:
                    value_7 = -jnp.inf
                else:

                    else:
                        standard_logccdf = _standard_logccdf(logccdf_z, value_4 > -np.log(2))
                        value_6 = standard_logccdf
                    value_7 = value_6
                a = value_7
                log_scale_3 = np.log(0.2)
                if (1.0 == 0.5 if 0.2 == 0 else False):
                    value_8 = 1.0 / 0.2
                else:
                    standardized_2_2 = _standardized_2(0.5, 0.2, log_scale_3, 1.0, value_4 > -np.log(2))
                    value_8 = standardized_2_2
                logccdf_z_2 = value_8
                if 1.0 == jnp.inf:

                else:

                    else:

                        value_9 = standard_logccdf_2
                    value_10 = value_9
                b = value_10
                return jax.lax.cond(a == b, lambda: -jnp.inf, lambda: a + _rk_log1mexp(b - a))
            def else_arm():
                log_scale_4 = np.log(0.2)

                    if 1.0 == jnp.inf:
                        value_12 = 0.0
                    else:
                        standard_logcdf_2 = _standard_logcdf_2(logcdf_z_2, jnp.logical_not(value_4 > -np.log(2)))
                        value_12 = standard_logcdf_2
                    value_13 = value_12
                a_2 = value_13
                log_scale_5 = np.log(0.2)
                if (0.0 == 0.5 if 0.2 == 0 else False):
                    value_14 = 1.0 / 0.2
                else:
                    standardized_3_2 = _standardized_3(0.5, 0.2, log_scale_5, 0.0, jnp.logical_not(value_4 > -np.log(2)))
                    value_14 = standardized_3_2
                logcdf_z_3 = value_14
                if 0.0 == -jnp.inf:
                    value_16 = -jnp.inf
                else:
                    if 0.0 == jnp.inf:

                    else:

                        value_15 = standard_logcdf_2_2
                    value_16 = value_15
                b_2 = value_16
                return jax.lax.cond(a_2 == b_2, lambda: -jnp.inf, lambda: a_2 + _rk_log1mexp(b_2 - a_2))
            value_17 = jax.lax.cond(value_4 > -np.log(2), then_arm, else_arm)
        ppl_prior_beta = ppl_prior_beta_logpdf + -value_17
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_sigma",)):

    if "ppl_scan_rest_level" in outputs:

def viral_shedding_trajectory(t_peak: ArrayLike, viral_peak: ArrayLike, duration_shedding: ArrayLike, n: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `viral_shedding_trajectory` from its authored source."""
    def _deffun_julia_alloc() -> jax.Array:
        """Compute `_deffun_julia_alloc` from its authored source."""
        return jnp.zeros(((n,)[0],), dtype=jnp.float64)
    deffun_julia_alloc = _deffun_julia_alloc()
    s = deffun_julia_alloc
    growth = viral_peak / t_peak
    wane = viral_peak / (duration_shedding - t_peak)
    def loop_body(t, carry):
        (s_2,) = carry
        def then_arm():
            s_3 = s_2.at[t - 1].set(jnp.exp(np.log(10.0) * growth * t))
            return (None, s_3)
        def else_arm():
            log10_load = viral_peak + wane * t_peak - wane * t
            s_4 = s_2.at[t - 1].set(jnp.exp(np.log(10.0) * jnp.where(log10_load < 0.0, 0.0, log10_load)))
            return (None, s_4)
        branch = jax.lax.cond(t <= t_peak, then_arm, else_arm)
        return (branch[1],)
    carry_init = (s,)
    loop_carry = jax.lax.fori_loop(1, n + 1, loop_body, carry_init) if 1 <= n else carry_init
    return loop_carry[0] / jnp.sum(loop_carry[0])

def _rk_lgamma_correction(x):
    # log(gamma(x)) - ((x - 0.5) * log(x) - x + 0.5 * log(2 pi)), for x >= 10:
    # the Stirling series through x^-15.
    z = 1.0 / (x * x)
    return (1.0 / x) * (1.0 / 12 + z * (-1.0 / 360 + z * (1.0 / 1260 + z * (-1.0 / 1680
        + z * (1.0 / 1188 + z * (-691.0 / 360360 + z * (1.0 / 156 + z * (-3617.0 / 122400))))))))


def _rk_logbeta_np(a, b):
    # SpecialFunctions.logbeta for positive arguments. With b the larger, a
    # large b subtracts log(gamma(b)) - log(gamma(a + b)) in Stirling form,
    # without cancellation.
    a, b = np.minimum(a, b), np.maximum(a, b)
    small = ssp.gammaln(a) + ssp.gammaln(b) - ssp.gammaln(a + b)
    big = np.maximum(b, 10.0)
    large = (ssp.gammaln(a) + _rk_lgamma_correction(big) - _rk_lgamma_correction(a + big)
             - (a + big - 0.5) * np.log1p(a / big) - a * np.log(big) + a)
    return np.where(b < 10, small, large)


def _check_slice_vector_arg(what: ArrayLike, a: ArrayLike, groups: ArrayLike, k: ArrayLike) -> Any:
    """Compute `_check_slice_vector_arg` from its authored source."""
    if not (a.size == k):
        raise ValueError("".join([str(what), str(" has slices of ")]) + "".join([str("length "), str(a.size), str(", but the declared slices have length "), str(k)]))
    n = None
    return None


@jax.custom_jvp
def _loggamma(x1):
    return jsp.gammaln(x1)


def _loggamma_partials_1(x1):
    return (jsp.gammaln(x1), jsp.digamma(x1))


def _loggamma_jvp(primals, tangents):
    active = tuple(not isinstance(t, jax.custom_derivatives.SymbolicZero) for t in tangents)
    mask = sum((1 << i) for i, a in enumerate(active) if a)
    if mask == 0:
        value = _loggamma(*primals)
        return value, jnp.zeros_like(value)
    if mask == 1:
        values = _loggamma_partials_1(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[0]
_loggamma.defjvp(_loggamma_jvp, symbolic_zeros=True)


def _ScalarDerivativeRule(x1):
    value = _loggamma(x1)
    return value


def brm_group_effects_density(
    ppl_last_z: ArrayLike,
    tau: ArrayLike,
    unconstrained: ArrayLike,
    *,
    outputs: tuple[str, ...],
) -> dict:
    """Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

    Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
    `z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
    level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
    """
    results = {}
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_arrflat_z", "ppl_prior_z", "ppl_pw_prior_z")):
        ppl_arrflat_z = unconstrained[37:ppl_last_z]
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_tau", "ppl_pw_prior_tau")):
        def ppl_pw_prior_tau_cell(tau_2):
            log_scale = np.log(0.75)
            standardized = (tau_2 - 0.0) / jnp.where((tau_2 == 0.0 if 0.75 == 0 else False), 1.0, 0.75)
            standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * standardized ** 2
            logpdf = standard_logpdf - jnp.where((tau_2 != 0.0 if 0.75 == 0 else False), 0.0, log_scale)
            return logpdf
        ppl_pw_prior_tau = (jnp.zeros(tau.shape[:1], dtype=jnp.float64) if 0 in tau.shape[:1] else jax.vmap(ppl_pw_prior_tau_cell, in_axes=(0,))(tau))
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_tau",)):
        ppl_prior_tau = jnp.sum(ppl_pw_prior_tau)
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_z", "ppl_pw_prior_z")):
        def ppl_pw_prior_z_cell(z):
            log_scale = np.log(1.0)
            standardized = (z - 0.0) / jnp.where((z == 0.0 if 1.0 == 0 else False), 1.0, 1.0)
            standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * standardized ** 2
            logpdf = standard_logpdf - jnp.where((z != 0.0 if 1.0 == 0 else False), 0.0, log_scale)
            return logpdf
        ppl_pw_prior_z = (jnp.zeros(ppl_arrflat_z.shape[:1], dtype=jnp.float64) if 0 in ppl_arrflat_z.shape[:1] else jax.vmap(ppl_pw_prior_z_cell, in_axes=(0,))(ppl_arrflat_z))
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_z",)):
        ppl_prior_z = jnp.sum(ppl_pw_prior_z)
    if "ppl_arrflat_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_arrflat_z"] = ppl_arrflat_z
    if "ppl_prior_tau" in outputs:
        results["ppl_prior_tau"] = ppl_prior_tau
    if "ppl_prior_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_prior_z"] = ppl_prior_z
    if "ppl_pw_prior_tau" in outputs:
        results["ppl_pw_prior_tau"] = ppl_pw_prior_tau
    if "ppl_pw_prior_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_pw_prior_z"] = ppl_pw_prior_z
    return results

def _rk_check(valid, message):
    # ReactiveKernels._runtime_check: raises when the program runs on values
    # that fail the check.
    def check(v):
        import numpy as np
        if not np.all(v):
            raise ValueError(message)
    # A plate checks all active lanes with one callback. Re-entering checked
    # batches outer vmap axes too; an empty axis executes no checks.
    @jax.custom_batching.custom_vmap
    def checked(v):
        jax.debug.callback(check, v)
        return ()
    @checked.def_vmap
    def checked_batch(axis_size, in_batched, v):
        if axis_size:
            checked(jnp.all(v))
        return (), ()
    checked(valid)


def jcall(unused: ArrayLike, unused_2: ArrayLike, x: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `jcall` from its Julia definition."""
    return x * x


def ar1_dev(eps: ArrayLike, eps_lengths: ArrayLike, phi: ArrayLike, sigma: ArrayLike) -> tuple:
    """Compute `ar1_dev` from its authored source."""
    nt = eps_lengths
    def _deffun_julia_alloc_2() -> tuple:
        """Compute `_deffun_julia_alloc` from its authored source."""
        _rk_check(((nt,)[0] >= 0), "ArgumentError: negative array dimension")
        return (jnp.zeros(((eps.shape[0],)[0],), dtype=jnp.float64), (nt,)[0])
    deffun_julia_alloc_2 = _deffun_julia_alloc_2()
    d = deffun_julia_alloc_2[0]
    jcall_2 = jcall(None, None, phi)
    d_2 = d.at[0].set(sigma * eps[0] / jnp.sqrt(1.0 - jcall_2))
    reach = nt - 2
    def loop_body(step, carry):
        kept = step <= reach
        def step_body(carry_2):
            (d_3,) = carry_2
            t = jnp.minimum(2 + step, nt)
            d_4 = d_3.at[t - 1].set(phi * d_3[t - 1 - 1] + sigma * eps[t - 1])
            return (d_4,)
        return jax.lax.cond(kept, step_body, lambda c: c, carry)
    carry_init = (d_2,)
    loop_carry = jax.lax.fori_loop(0, max(eps.shape[0] - 2 + 1, 0), loop_body, carry_init) if 1 <= max(eps.shape[0] - 2 + 1, 0) else carry_init

def renewal_feedback(logRt: ArrayLike, logRt_lengths: ArrayLike, g: ArrayLike, gamma: ArrayLike, I0: ArrayLike, r: ArrayLike, n_seed: ArrayLike) -> tuple:
    """Compute `renewal_feedback` from its authored source."""
    nt = logRt_lengths
    ng = g.shape[0]
    def _deffun_julia_alloc_3() -> tuple:
        """Compute `_deffun_julia_alloc` from its authored source."""
        _rk_check(((nt,)[0] >= 0), "ArgumentError: negative array dimension")

    deffun_julia_alloc_3 = _deffun_julia_alloc_3()
    I = deffun_julia_alloc_3[0]
    reach = nt - 1
    def loop_body(step, carry):
        kept = step <= reach
        def step_body(carry_2):
            (I_2,) = carry_2
            t = jnp.minimum(1 + step, nt)
            def then_arm():
                I_3 = I_2.at[t - 1].set(I0 * jnp.exp(r * (t - 1)))
                return (None, I_3)
            def else_arm():
                conv = 0.0
                def loop_body_2(s, carry_3):
                    (conv_2,) = carry_3
                    prev = jax.lax.cond(t - s >= 1, lambda: I_2[t - s - 1], lambda: 0.0)
                    conv_3 = conv_2 + g[s - 1] * prev

                loop_carry = jax.lax.fori_loop(1, ng + 1, loop_body_2, carry_init) if 1 <= ng else carry_init

                I_4 = I_2.at[t - 1].set(Rt * loop_carry[0])

            branch = jax.lax.cond(t <= n_seed, then_arm, else_arm)
            return (branch[1],)

    loop_carry = jax.lax.fori_loop(0, max(logRt.shape[0] - 1 + 1, 0), loop_body, carry_init) if 1 <= max(logRt.shape[0] - 1 + 1, 0) else carry_init
    last_valid = jnp.maximum(deffun_julia_alloc_3[1] - 1, 0)
    padded = loop_carry[0]
    padded_2 = (padded if padded.shape[0] == 0 else jnp.where((jnp.arange(padded.shape[0]) < deffun_julia_alloc_3[1]), padded, jax.lax.dynamic_index_in_dim(padded, last_valid, 0, keepdims=True)))
    return (padded_2, deffun_julia_alloc_3[1])


def renewal_from_first_observed(logRt: ArrayLike, logRt_lengths: ArrayLike, g: ArrayLike, gamma: ArrayLike, i_first_obs: ArrayLike, growth: ArrayLike, uot: ArrayLike) -> tuple:

def brm_group_effects_density_3(
    ppl_first_z: ArrayLike,
    ppl_last_z: ArrayLike,
    tau: ArrayLike,
    unconstrained: ArrayLike,
    *,
    outputs: tuple[str, ...],
) -> dict:
    """Group-level (varying) effects of grouping `g`.

    Non-centered, from the scale `tau[1]` (drawn from its prior) and standardized effects
    `z[1:length(levels(g)), 1:1] ~ Normal(0, 1)`. Returns the
    level-by-margin matrix `z .* tau[1]`, one row per level of `g` in order.
    """
    results = {}
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_arrflat_z", "ppl_prior_z", "ppl_pw_prior_z")):
        ppl_arrflat_z = unconstrained[ppl_first_z - 1:ppl_last_z]
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_tau", "ppl_pw_prior_tau")):
        def ppl_pw_prior_tau_cell(tau_2):
            log_scale = np.log(0.5)
            standardized = (tau_2 - 0.0) / jnp.where((tau_2 == 0.0 if 0.5 == 0 else False), 1.0, 0.5)
            standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * standardized ** 2
            logpdf = standard_logpdf - jnp.where((tau_2 != 0.0 if 0.5 == 0 else False), 0.0, log_scale)
            return logpdf
        ppl_pw_prior_tau = (jnp.zeros(tau.shape[:1], dtype=jnp.float64) if 0 in tau.shape[:1] else jax.vmap(ppl_pw_prior_tau_cell, in_axes=(0,))(tau))
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_tau",)):
        ppl_prior_tau = jnp.sum(ppl_pw_prior_tau)
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_z", "ppl_pw_prior_z")):
        def ppl_pw_prior_z_cell(z):
            log_scale = np.log(1.0)
            standardized = (z - 0.0) / jnp.where((z == 0.0 if 1.0 == 0 else False), 1.0, 1.0)
            standard_logpdf = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * standardized ** 2
            logpdf = standard_logpdf - jnp.where((z != 0.0 if 1.0 == 0 else False), 0.0, log_scale)
            return logpdf
        ppl_pw_prior_z = (jnp.zeros(ppl_arrflat_z.shape[:1], dtype=jnp.float64) if 0 in ppl_arrflat_z.shape[:1] else jax.vmap(ppl_pw_prior_z_cell, in_axes=(0,))(ppl_arrflat_z))
    if any(name in outputs for name in ("ppl_prior_z",)):
        ppl_prior_z = jnp.sum(ppl_pw_prior_z)
    if "ppl_arrflat_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_arrflat_z"] = ppl_arrflat_z
    if "ppl_prior_tau" in outputs:
        results["ppl_prior_tau"] = ppl_prior_tau
    if "ppl_prior_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_prior_z"] = ppl_prior_z
    if "ppl_pw_prior_tau" in outputs:
        results["ppl_pw_prior_tau"] = ppl_pw_prior_tau
    if "ppl_pw_prior_z" in outputs:
        results["ppl_pw_prior_z"] = ppl_pw_prior_z
    return results

def _logrising_product_domain(a: ArrayLike, m: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:

def _logrising_product(a: ArrayLike, m: ArrayLike, partial: ArrayLike) -> tuple:
    """Compute `_logrising_product` from its authored source."""
    chunk = (32 if 1.7976931348623157e308 > 3.4028234663852886e38 else jnp.where(a + m <= 256, jnp.asarray(16, dtype=jnp.int64), jnp.asarray(4, dtype=jnp.int64)))
    L = jnp.zeros_like(a)
    D = jnp.zeros_like(a)
    j = 0
    loop_test = j < m
    def loop_body(carry):
        (D_2, L_2, j_2, _) = carry
        stop = jnp.minimum(m, j_2 + chunk)
        P1 = jnp.ones_like(a)
        P2 = jnp.ones_like(a)
        P3 = jnp.ones_like(a)
        P4 = jnp.ones_like(a)
        d1 = jnp.zeros_like(a)
        d2 = jnp.zeros_like(a)
        d3 = jnp.zeros_like(a)
        d4 = jnp.zeros_like(a)
        loop_test_2 = j_2 + 3 < stop
        def loop_body_2(carry_2):
            (P1_2, P2_2, P3_2, P4_2, d1_2, d2_2, d3_2, d4_2, j_3, _) = carry_2
            x1 = a + j_3
            x2 = x1 + 1
            x3 = x1 + 2
            x4 = x1 + 3
            if partial:
                d1_3 = d1_2 * x1 + P1_2
                d2_3 = d2_2 * x2 + P2_2
                d3_3 = d3_2 * x3 + P3_2
                d4_3 = d4_2 * x4 + P4_2
                value = (None, jnp.asarray(d1_3, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d2_3, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d3_3, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d4_3, dtype=jnp.float64))
            else:
                value = (None, jnp.asarray(d1_2, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d2_2, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d3_2, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d4_2, dtype=jnp.float64))
            P1_3 = P1_2 * x1
            P2_3 = P2_2 * x2
            P3_3 = P3_2 * x3
            P4_3 = P4_2 * x4
            j_4 = j_3 + 4
            return (P1_3, P2_3, P3_3, P4_3, value[1], value[2], value[3], value[4], j_4, j_4 + 3 < stop)
        loop_carry = jax.lax.while_loop(lambda carry: carry[-1], loop_body_2, (jnp.asarray(P1, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(P2, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(P3, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(P4, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d1, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d2, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d3, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(d4, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(j_2, dtype=jnp.int64), loop_test_2))
        loop_test_3 = loop_carry[8] < stop
        def loop_body_3(carry_3):
            (P1_2, d1_2, j_3, _) = carry_3
            x1 = a + j_3
            if partial:
                d1_3 = d1_2 * x1 + P1_2
                value = (None, jnp.asarray(d1_3, dtype=jnp.float64))
            else:
                value = (None, jnp.asarray(d1_2, dtype=jnp.float64))
            P1_3 = P1_2 * x1
            j_4 = j_3 + 1
            return (P1_3, value[1], j_4, j_4 < stop)
        loop_carry_2 = jax.lax.while_loop(lambda carry: carry[-1], loop_body_3, (jnp.asarray(loop_carry[0], dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(loop_carry[4], dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(loop_carry[8], dtype=jnp.int64), loop_test_3))
        P12 = loop_carry_2[0] * loop_carry[1]
        P34 = loop_carry[2] * loop_carry[3]
        L_3 = L_2 + jnp.log(P12 * P34)
        if partial:
            d12 = loop_carry_2[1] * loop_carry[1] + loop_carry[5] * loop_carry_2[0]
            d34 = loop_carry[6] * loop_carry[3] + loop_carry[7] * loop_carry[2]
            D_3 = D_2 + (d12 * P34 + d34 * P12) / (P12 * P34)
            value = (None, jnp.asarray(D_3, dtype=jnp.float64))
        else:
            value = (None, jnp.asarray(D_2, dtype=jnp.float64))
        return (value[1], L_3, loop_carry_2[2], loop_carry_2[2] < m)
    loop_carry = jax.lax.while_loop(lambda carry: carry[-1], loop_body, (jnp.asarray(D, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(L, dtype=jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(j, dtype=jnp.int64), loop_test))
    return ((loop_carry[1], loop_carry[0]),)


def _logrising_gamma_value(a: ArrayLike, m: ArrayLike, active: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:

def _logrising_value(a: ArrayLike, m: ArrayLike) -> jax.Array:
    """Compute `_logrising_value` from its authored source."""
    logrising_product_domain = _logrising_product_domain(a, m)
    product = logrising_product_domain
    count = jax.lax.cond(product, lambda: m, lambda: jnp.zeros_like(m))
    logrising_product = _logrising_product(a, count, False)
    rising = logrising_product[0][0]
    def else_arm():
        logrising_gamma_value = _logrising_gamma_value(a, m, jnp.logical_not(product))
        return logrising_gamma_value
    return jax.lax.cond(product, lambda: rising, else_arm)

    return logrising_value

def _logrising_jvp(primals, tangents):
    active = tuple(not isinstance(t, jax.custom_derivatives.SymbolicZero) for t in tangents)
    mask = sum((1 << i) for i, a in enumerate(active) if a)
    if mask == 0:
        value = _logrising(*primals)
        return value, jnp.zeros_like(value)
    if mask == 1:
        values = _logrising_partials_1(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[0]
    if mask == 2:
        values = _logrising_partials_2(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[1]
    if mask == 3:
        values = _logrising_partials_3(*primals)
        return values[0], values[1] * tangents[0] + values[2] * tangents[1]
_logrising.defjvp(_logrising_jvp, symbolic_zeros=True)


def _rk_bound_span(first, last):
    """The largest `last - first` of two prepared integer arrays' entries at one
    position (over the positions both have), static: the steps of the longest
    range `first[i]:last[i]`, less one (-1 without entries).
    """
    first, last = np.asarray(first), np.asarray(last)
    if first.ndim != last.ndim:
        return StaticInt((int(last.max()) if last.size else 0) -
                         (int(first.min()) if first.size else 0))
    block = tuple(slice(0, min(m, n)) for m, n in zip(first.shape, last.shape))
    d = last[block] - first[block]
    return StaticInt(int(d.max()) if d.size else -1)

    return model("log_density", unconstrained, **prepared)

    return model("log_prior", unconstrained, **prepared)

    return model("log_likelihood", unconstrained, **prepared)

Wastewater concentration is proportional to infection incidence convolved with the shedding profile. The profile has an inferred peak and duration and is normalized before convolution. A laboratory multiplier changes the concentration scale, and a laboratory noise scale controls log-concentration error. Values at their detection limits contribute a left-censoring probability. Concentrations retain their source units, genome copies per mL; the dilution constant uses mL per person per day.

Hospital admissions constrain a different view of the same infections. The model averages incidence with population weights, convolves it with the infection-to-hospital delay distribution, and applies a varying admission probability and a mean-one weekday effect. A negative-binomial likelihood accounts for count variation beyond the Poisson variance. The wastewater and admission frames remain separate throughout this calculation; there is no interpolation of sparse samples into invented daily measurements.

With one measured catchment, the state admissions series supplies information about infections outside that catchment. The shared reference and deviation priors determine how those signals are pooled. Changing the population weights therefore changes the scientific model, not merely the labels on its output.

Fit and diagnostics ​

Four independent WarmupHMC chains start from different random seeds, each requesting 1,000 retained draws. The completion sampler requires three chains to finish and then lets the remaining chain finish its current warmup round. The table records how many chains contributed, which were omitted, the total retained draws, divergences and sampling time. These are results of the cached run; rebuilding this page reads its tables without sampling again.

startedretainedomitteddrawsdivergences%seconds
4313000200.6667517.4

Population summaries use the retained chains on the quantities' natural scales. The intervals contain the central 95 % of their pooled draws. Split R-hat compares chains; bulk and tail effective sample sizes describe the information in the centre and tails. A small divergence count alone is insufficient evidence that the chains agree. The completion rule can also select chains by speed, so the omitted-chain record belongs with the result.

This run retained three chains and recorded 20 divergences. The initial reference reproduction number has R-hat 1.084 and bulk ESS 49, so agreement on the other reported quantities does not establish convergence of the whole fit. The initial level belongs to the unobserved seeding history, but its uncertainty is coupled to the later trajectory. Treat the bands below as provisional Monte Carlo summaries, not validated transmission estimates.

The plotted quantity is the exponentiated shared reference process, before infection feedback and catchment-specific deviations. It is not the realized reproduction number of the measured catchment. Its bands describe uncertainty in that latent reference, rather than a prediction interval for a future concentration. Convolution and sparse sampling mean that a short change in wastewater need not imply an equally sharp change in transmission.

This example uses BRM's structural port of the CDC model. The recurrence, subpopulation hierarchy, shedding and count streams follow the same causal order; the priors and hospitalization-rate parameterization are those of the checked-in BRM declaration. This fit is not a reproduction of CDC's posterior estimates. The research notes give the differences and retain the smaller EpiSewer-style model for comparison.

Reproduce ​

Commands and fit receipt

The repository's test environment supplies the pinned BRM, StanBlocks, BridgeStan, WarmupHMC and TreeArrays dependencies. These shell commands are manual: the docs build executes the model declarations and figures but reads the completed fit's summaries. Run the fit deliberately when its model, data or settings change; routine documentation edits reuse the cache.

sh
julia --startup-file=no --project=test test/setup_env.jl
julia -t 4 --startup-file=no --project=test research/wastewater/fit.jl

The script writes its receipt before sampling and saves the draws outside the repository. Its key includes the emitted program, data, settings, seed and sampling harness. TreeArrays reduces the named chain and draw axes to small summary tables. A second invocation with the same key rebuilds those tables from the saved draws. The receipt identifies the program behind these numbers.

On a fresh checkout the draws may be absent. An existing receipt guards against repeating a recent fit; set BRM_DOCS_FIT_FORCE=1 for a deliberate rerun. BRM_DOCS_CACHE selects a persistent draw-cache directory; its default is under the system temporary directory. Only the small summary tables belong in git.
